observed_reality.pr557_scope: Connection-bound database-object topology guard using SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED for rename/move/delete/rebind detection; productive persistence and whole state integrity are not claimed.
observed_reality.upstream_hasmoved_semantics: SQLite documents SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED as reporting whether the opened file has been renamed, moved, or deleted since first open.
observed_reality.upstream_application_id_layout: SQLite documents the four-byte big-endian application_id field at database-header offset 68.
observed_reality.pr557_current_ci_at_cycle: Current head workflow Frank SQLite connection guard v1 was PENDING at observation; a previous-head run was CANCELLED and is not promoted.

generated_reality.hypothesis: A connection can continue to report HAS_MOVED=0 after same-inode database content drift because the opcode is a topology discriminator, not a content-integrity witness.
generated_reality.strongest_counterhypothesis: The serving connection's HAS_MOVED/file-object binding is sufficient to treat the opened database state as unchanged for release acceptance.

bounded_unusual_experiment.name: HAS_MOVED_SAME_INODE_CONTENT_DRIFT
bounded_unusual_experiment.scope: Disposable local C/SQLite WAL fixture only; no Frank/VPS/canonical/product database, provider effect, Harness authority or training state mutated.

control.setup: Open database, enable WAL, create table, insert one row, execute wal_checkpoint(FULL), then query SQLITE_FCNTL_HAS_MOVED on the live main connection.

treatment.intervention: While the original SQLite connection stayed open, independently open the same database pathname O_RDWR, pwrite bytes 01 02 03 04 at header offset 68 (application_id), fsync, close.

acceptance_delta.requirement: Do not promote connection-bound HAS_MOVED success into content/state-integrity truth. Accepted-Hostinger evidence must independently bind productive transactional/recovery semantics and any required database-file authority/content-change expectations.
acceptance_delta.reason_no_parallel_product_pr: PR #557 already states a narrow rename/move/delete/rebind scope; this finding refines the acceptance/non-claim boundary rather than identifying a defect requiring duplicate implementation.

negative_results_and_limits: No accepted Hostinger ProductStart or productive UnifiedDB persistence path was exercised.
The experiment does not establish malicious or ordinary product reachability of same-inode external writes.
The local runtime was SQLite 3.46.1; this experiment tests HAS_MOVED semantic scope, not the WAL-reset bug fix boundary or accepted 3.53.4 identity.
PR #557 remains DRAFT and its exact current-head CI was not PASS at this evidence point.
No whole F-V01-13 or Frank v0.1 acceptance claim is made.
next_falsifier: On the accepted Hostinger ProductStart/self.root generation, bind exact fixed SQLite runtime + exact live connection/database object + real UnifiedDB transaction and recovery receipts, then show fail-closed behavior for the specified rollback/downgrade/library-swap/topology controls without treating HAS_MOVED as a content-integrity oracle.
